legs.name: clippy
legs.extract: select(.reason == "compiler-message") | select(.message.level == "error" or .message.level == "warning") | {type: "clippy", level: .message.level, file: ([.message.spans[]? | select(.is_primary)][0].file_name // .message.spans[0]?.file_name // "unknown"), line: ([.message.spans[]? | select(.is_primary)][0].line_start // .message.spans[0]?.line_start // null), lint: (.message.code.code // "compile-error"), message: .message.message}

legs.name: blocking-call-in-native-bif
legs.note: Wrapped in a script because the BARE `ast-grep scan` returns its PASSING verdict (empty findings, rc 0) in two failure states, both measured: an emptied rule pattern list, and a scan path that does not exist -- the latter prints 'No such file or directory' to STDERR while still exiting 0, so even capturing stderr does not fail the leg. A missing rule FILE does exit nonzero (rc 6) and was already safe. beamr has restructured src/ directories twice recently, so a renamed native/ would have left this gate scanning nothing and reporting clean forever. The script establishes that the checker CAN fire (positive-control fixtures under .ast-grep/fixtures/, requiring one hit per declared pattern, so an untested new pattern fails the gate) and that the scan path exists and holds >=1 .rs file, BEFORE believing an empty result. Line numbers in ast-grep's --json output are ZERO-INDEXED while its human report style is one-indexed: a finding printed as line 212 appears as "line": 211 here. Do not chase a phantom off-by-one. The script parses the JSON count rather than trusting exit codes, and never suppresses stderr -- the 'N error(s) found' notice during the positive control is EXPECTED and is announced on the line above it.
